brief: Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid runs a chart from his new chartbook, The Home Straight, built on Binky Chadha and Parag Thatte's review of Q2 global earnings. The chart shows S&P 500 earnings per share growing inside a stable long-term channel at around 6.5% annually, with the Great Depression, the post-war boom, the tech revolution, globalisation and the internet era all staying within those boundaries. US earnings are now breaking out on the upside of that channel, and Chadha and Thatte expect that to be sustained in the quarters ahead. If sustained, Reid says it would be one of the most significant structural breaks in modern market history, with recent years helped enormously by AI. His caveat is that the chart tracks EPS, not aggregate corporate profits, so a shrinking share count from buybacks can lift it and heavy issuance can dilute it. Against that, Thatte's read is that the buyback impact peaked in the 2010s, before the breakout, and that over the last 60 years raw S&P 500 earnings grew faster than EPS. Reid does not resolve it, framing the choice as an AI-driven sustainable breakout against an earnings bubble as the capex boom lifts all boats.
